name: ManageEngine Endpoint Central
description: ManageEngine Endpoint Central is a unified endpoint management and security platform that patches, secures, and manages Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and Chrome OS devices from a single console.
best_for: IT teams that need to manage and secure a genuinely mixed fleet of Windows, Mac, Linux, and mobile devices from one console with published, self-serve per-endpoint pricing.
features: Automated patch management across Windows, macOS, Linux, and third-party applications, with compliance auditing against 130+ CIS benchmarks
Software distribution, application control, and OS imaging/deployment
IT asset management with hardware/software inventory and license and warranty tracking
Remote troubleshooting and remote desktop sharing
Ransomware protection with root-cause analysis, data loss prevention, and endpoint privilege management
Next-generation antivirus and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR)
Mobile device management across iOS, iPadOS, Android, and Chrome OS, a Secure Private Access module, and Zia AI automation for routine tasks like vulnerability triage and patch rollout
pros: Genuinely cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, Chrome OS) from one console, unlike Apple-only or Windows-centric tools
Published, self-serve numeric pricing by endpoint count for both cloud and on-premises deployment
30-day free trial that manages unlimited endpoints, no credit card required
cons: Pricing is banded by edition (Professional/Enterprise/UEM/Security) and endpoint volume, and several security capabilities (EDR, malware protection, ransomware protection, DEX, Secure Private Access) are separately priced add-ons rather than included in the base price
No permanent free edition is currently advertised -- only a time-limited free trial

tiers.name: Professional (Cloud)
tiers.notes: Or $1,045/year billed annually. On-premises licensing is also available ($795/year annual, or $1,987 one-time perpetual plus 20% annual maintenance). Price scales with endpoint count (bands published up to 10,000 endpoints); Professional is one of four editions (Professional/Enterprise/UEM/Security) -- see official source for UEM/Security editions and the exact figure at your scale.

tiers.name: Enterprise (Cloud)
tiers.notes: Or $1,245/year billed annually. Same endpoint-volume and on-premises/cloud structure as Professional, at a higher per-endpoint rate for additional Enterprise-tier features.

alternatives.name: Jamf Pro
alternatives.description: Jamf Pro is Apple-only device management software for deploying, configuring, securing, and patching Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV devices.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations that manage Apple devices exclusively or near-exclusively and want Apple-native depth over broad cross-platform coverage.
strengths: Apple ecosystem integrations (Entra, Okta, Google Workspace)

alternatives.name: NinjaOne
alternatives.description: NinjaOne is a unified IT operations platform combining RMM, patch management, backup, remote access, and service-desk ticketing for IT teams and MSPs.
alternatives.best_for: MSPs and IT teams wanting RMM and ticketing bundled together, with quote-based pricing rather than a published per-endpoint price table.
strengths: Unified RMM, backup, and remote access

faq.question: Does ManageEngine Endpoint Central publish its pricing?
faq.answer: Yes. Unlike many RMM/UEM tools in this category, Endpoint Central publishes a full self-serve pricing table by edition (Professional, Enterprise, UEM, Security), endpoint/server count, and deployment type (cloud or on-premises). As of the last verified date, the Professional cloud plan starts at $104/month for 50 endpoints with 1 technician.
